Key Research Thinking Patterns: Multi-Modal Sensor Fusion: Integrating disparate remote sensing data streams, such as NEXRAD radar and LunAero moonwatching systems, with deep learning object detection (Faster R-CNN) to automate the identification and tracking of biological scatterers in complex atmospheric environments.

Spatiotemporal Environmental Attribution: Utilizing sliding window regression and spatially explicit time-window analyses on NCEP reanalysis data to isolate and quantify the impact of local and teleconnected climate variables on migratory timing and phenology.

Behavioral State Segmentation: Applying Hidden Markov Models (HMM) and unsupervised clustering to satellite telemetry data (Movebank) to delineate ecologically distinct migratory groups and define specific behavioral states such as commuting, foraging, and roosting.

Community Science Triangulation: Validating automated computational detections against human-curated citizen science datasets (eBird, MartinRoost) to resolve taxonomic ambiguity and confirm the biological significance of large-scale communal roosting events.
Summary Description: Jeffrey Kelley specializes in aeroecology and movement ecology, leveraging advanced computational methods to monitor avian migration and inform conservation strategies. By integrating NEXRAD radar, LunAero moonwatching, and satellite telemetry with deep learning pipelines (Faster R-CNN) and Hidden Markov Models, he quantifies population trends and behavioral dynamics of aerial insectivores and shorebirds. His research bridges computer vision and climate science, utilizing spatiotemporal analyses of reanalysis data to elucidate climate-driven phenological shifts. Furthermore, Kelley pioneers a Community Science-Radar Triangulation framework, validating automated detections against citizen science data to resolve taxonomic ambiguities. This holistic approach provides continent-scale insights into migratory connectivity and habitat selection, offering critical tools for managing declining species under changing environmental conditions.
